resources.string: Hotspot on for “%1$s”. Keep this screen nearby.
No deployments yet. Create one to get started.
Trainers use this PIN to unlock the settings screen on a device. Write it down: it cannot be read back from here.
The PIN is already set. Type a new one only if you want to change it.
Ticked apps are installed and protected. Use the second tick to also show an app on the home screen — an app can be installed as a share target without appearing there.
Off is the normal setting. The battery and signal icons stay visible, but the shade cannot be pulled down, so mobile data and airplane mode cannot be changed by accident.
Turning this on has three costs:
Add apps in the Apps tab first.
Devices join these networks on their own. Add the team\'s sync network here — people using a device cannot add one themselves without the admin PIN.
Password (leave empty for an open network)
Saved this deployment to the file you chose.
That deployment could not be saved there. Choose another folder and try again.
That file could not be read. Choose the deployment file you were sent.
That file is not a deployment. Choose the file a colleague exported from this app.
No apps yet. Add the APK files you want to install on devices.
Check this matches what you expect before deploying to a whole team. A device will refuse an app whose fingerprint does not match.
On the new phone, tap the first screen six times, then scan this code.
The phone must be freshly reset, and running Android 9 or newer.
Stop and turn off the hotspot
All the devices you set up have reported back. It is safe to stop.
Set the hotspot up by hand
If this phone cannot start a hotspot on its own, turn on the hotspot in Settings, then type its name and password here.
To start its own hotspot this phone needs the nearby Wi-Fi permission. Allow it in Settings, or set the hotspot up by hand below.
This deployment does not fit in a code a phone camera can read reliably. Remove some apps, or shorten the deployment name.
Allow this by hand on the device: %1$s
This make of phone needs its battery settings changed by hand, or its apps will be stopped in the background.
1. Start a deployment on this phone. A square code appears.
2. Factory reset the new phone, or take it out of the box.
3. On its first “Hello” screen, tap the middle of the screen six times.
4. The phone opens a camera. Point it at the square code.
5. The phone joins this phone\'s hotspot and installs everything. Leave the two phones near each other.
6. When it finishes, the phone shows the kiosk home screen and appears in the list here.
Before you start, disconnect this phone from any Wi-Fi network. If it stays joined to one, the code can send the new phones to the wrong address and they will wait forever.
Bring a power bank. Running the hotspot and sending the apps drains this phone quickly — that, rather than speed, is what limits how many phones you can do in one go.
